top_evidence.document_title: Endoscopic submucosal dissection versus endoscopic mucosal resection for colorectal laterally spreading tumors (> 20 mm): a systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.section: Results > Statistical Analysis > Search Results And Population Characteristics
top_evidence.text: Statistical analyses were performed using the Cochrane Collaboration's RevMan 5.4 software. Statistical analyses were performed using the Cochrane Collaboration's RevMan 5.4 software. Data were analyzed using randomeffects models, with forest plots generated for each outcome. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Heterogeneity was assessed via Q -test and I 2 statistics. Sensitivity analysis employed the leave-one-out method to evaluate robustness. Publication bias was initially evaluated through funnel plot visualization and confirmed with Egger's test (Stata 18.0). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05 (heterogeneity threshold: p < 0.1). A total of 111 duplicate records were excluded using EndNote. After removing reviews, meta-analyses, letters, editorials, case reports/series, and ineligible publications, eight studies were ultimately included (see PRISMA flowchart, Fig. 1). The analysis comprised 3024 patients: 1451 underwent ESD and 1573 received EMR (including 588 piecemeal EMR procedures). Included studies consisted of one RCT and seven retrospective studies (six single-center, two multicenter), with geographical distribution as follows: three from South Korea, three from Japan, one from Germany, and one from France. Detailed study characteristics are summarized in Table 1. We used the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for nonrandomized studies to assess methodology quality, which gave a mean score of 7.7 (range 6-9) (Table 2) [18]. For the randomized trials, we used Cochrane's Risk of Bias assessment (Table 3) [19]. General characteristics of the studies and characteristics of the included lesions were shown in Table 1.

top_evidence.document_title: Endoscopic submucosal dissection versus endoscopic mucosal resection for colorectal laterally spreading tumors (> 20 mm): a systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.text: Background Colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) larger than 20 mm are significant precursors to colorectal cancer. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) and endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) are widely used treatments, but their comparative efficacy and safety remain controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare ESD and EMR in terms of local recurrence, perforation, and delayed bleeding for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases from inception to 1 May 2025. Studies comparing ESD and EMR for LSTs > 20 mm were included. Data were extracted and quality assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Eight studies comprising 3024 patients were included. ESD was associated with significantly lower local recurrence compared to EMR (0.62% versus 12.02%; OR 0.07, 95% CI 0.03-0.13, p < 0.01). However, ESD had a higher risk of perforation (5.38% versus 1.53%; OR 3.16, 95% CI 1.89-5.29, p < 0.01). No significant difference was found in delayed bleeding rates (3.65% versus 3.75%; OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.65-1.55, p = 0.98). Heterogeneity was negligible across all outcomes ( I 2 < 5%). Conclusions ESD significantly reduces recurrence risk for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm compared with EMR but carries a higher perforation risk. Bleeding rates are comparable between the two techniques. ESD is recommended in expert centers where technical proficiency can mitigate perforation risk, while EMR-treated patients require closer surveillance due to higher recurrence. Future studies should focus on optimizing techniques and clarifying strategies for different LST subtypes and locations. Keywords Neoplasms · Endoscopic mucosal resection · Endoscopic submucosal dissection · Recurrence · Complications

top_evidence.text: Most studies included in this meta-analysis were single-center or retrospective in nature. To minimize the risk of bias, we used the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale to assess the quality of nonrandomized studies. Furthermore, owing to missing original data, we were unable to compare the potential impact of different LST subtypes or lesion locations (e.g., proximal colon versus distal colon/rectum) on the efficacy and safety of the two techniques. Since different subtypes and locations may vary in biological behavior, technical difficulty, and prognosis (e.g., more advanced histology such as high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia or intramucosal carcinoma may increase the difficulty of en bloc resection), the absence of this information may affect the interpretation of the results. Future prospective, multicenter studies, especially those collecting detailed lesion characteristics, are needed to more comprehensively evaluate the value of ESD and EMR in different clinical scenarios. top_evidence.text: The GRADE working group approach was used to rate the quality of evidence. Based on the predominance of observational studies and negligible heterogeneity ( I 2 < 5%), the overall evidence was rated as low certainty. However, for local recurrence, the certainty was upgraded to moderate due to the very large magnitude of effect (OR 0.06).
